newsitem.title: LATVIA: Red Army monument damaged in Latvia blast.
newsitem.headline: Red Army monument damaged in Latvia blast.

text.p: A monument to Soviet Red Army troops who drove Nazi soldiers from the Latvian capital during World War Two was hit by a bomb blast on Friday, damaging the base of the needle-like column.
Russia's embassy reacted angrily to the blast, the first attack of its kind on the deeply symbolic Soviet-era monument, resented by Latvians but revered by local Russian-speakers.

"The explosion in the Victory Monument complex causes us great indignation. It is clear that this was not simply an act of vandalism but an intentional political action," Russian ambassador Alexander Udaltsov said in a statement.
"I think this action will not be left unanswered in Moscow," Udaltsov said.

Many Latvians want the 79-metre (259 feet) high Victory Monument column, flanked by huge statues of Red Army fighters, to be pulled down. They see it as a reminder of the 50 years they were forced to be part of the former Soviet Union until Latvia recovered its independence in 1991.
Local Russian-speaking inhabitants want the Red Army fighters to be honoured. It is often used as a meeting place for die-hard Communists and Soviet-era nostalgics.
The Latvian interior ministry said the base of the monument was damaged by a bomb of around 10 kg (22 lbs) operated by remote control just after midnight.
The white marble-style panelling was badly damaged and chunks of rubble were thrown over a wide distance. Windows of some nearby buildings were shattered.
An interior ministry spokesman said the police were investigating all theories, including whether the blast was aimed at damaging Latvian-Russian relations.
